title: Tracing playback & budget sync — 2026-04-16
body:
Meeting: Observability - trace playback & budget sync
Date: 2026-04-16 10:00 - 11:00 PT
Location: #eng-observability zoom / notes doc
Attendees: Elena K (owner), Ava M, Ravi P, Marcus C, Priya N, Samir G, plus drop-ins from Solutions Eng (Jun)

TL;DR
- Quick demo of trace-playback prototype: mostly there, needs deterministic span ordering for service X.
- Dashboard slowdowns traced to the BigQuery export job and an inefficient JOIN on the service metadata table.
- Cost telemetry spike in April traced to debug-mode ingestion toggles + very high sampling of health-check endpoints. Immediate mitigation: reduce sampling and enable server-side filtering for health checks.
- Action items assigned; main rollout on sampling changes targeted for 2026-04-22 canary.

Agenda
1) Playback prototype demo (Ravi)
2) Dashboard perf + query plan (Marcus)
3) Cost telemetry spike analysis (Ava / Priya)
4) Rollout plan and handoff checklist for next sprint (Elena)
5) Open questions + runbook updates

Notes
1) Playback prototype (Ravi)
- Demo: local playback of a 10k-span trace worked end-to-end; ordering preserved for single host traces but reordering occurs when trace contains concurrent spans from async workers.
- Root cause: the playback rehydrates spans based on recorded timestamp only; we lose the parent-child hints for async edges.
- Proposed fix: include synthetic parent-id mapping during export (see confluence page) and store an optional ordering token. This adds ~6% payload overhead but simplifies replay correctness.
- Risk: larger export size impacts ingestion cost (see cost section).

2) Dashboard perf (Marcus)
- Symptoms: dashboard panels using the trace-join report are timing out for 30-day windows.
- Root cause analysis: BigQuery query plan shows repeated JOINs on service_metadata (~200k rows) per execution; we are not using a pre-aggregated table for service-level dimensions.
- Short-term mitigation: create a daily materialized table with service_id -> metadata snapshot; change dashboards to reference it. Expected reduction in query time by ~70%.
- Medium-term: move heavy aggregations to scheduled precomputation (Lambda/Batch) and surface pre-aggregates to the dashboard backend.
- Ticket created: JIRA-OBS-4180 (dashboards: materialize service metadata).

3) Cost telemetry spike (Ava + Priya)
- April 9-12 spike: +38% ingestion egress cost driven by two factors: debug-mode traces (full payloads retained) and very high sampling on low-value routes (health-checks, heartbeat endpoints).
- Debug-mode flag found set true in staging/ops for longer than intended; patch to ensure debug-mode auto-expires (PR link in artifacts).
- Sampling anomaly: client-side sampling rate for health-checks was 10% in some regions due to a bad default override. Change default to 0.1% for ping endpoints.
- Cost math: reducing health-check sampling to 0.1% estimated to save ~18% of ingestion bytes at current traffic. Combined with debug-mode fix, total expected monthly savings: ~26-31% on trace ingestion line.

4) Rollout & Handoff (Elena)
- Plan: rollout sampling defaults + debug auto-expire in two phases: canary (region us-west-2) on 2026-04-22, full rollout 2026-04-29 if canary metrics stable.
- Monitoring: add canary metrics dashboard (simple KPIs: traces/sec, bytes/sec, error rate, span-drop-rate) and an automatic abort if ingestion latency > 200ms or bytes/sec drop > 40% unexpectedly.
- Handoff checklist for SRE/Oncall: update runbook, add escalation path to eng-observability, update cost alert thresholds.
- New runbook section: "trace-ingestion-budget-override" created, placeholder in Confluence.

Decisions made
- Implement synthetic parent-id mapping in export for playback correctness; accept ~6% payload overhead (decision owner: Ravi, due 2026-04-21).
- Materialize service metadata daily to fix dashboard joins (owner: Marcus, due 2026-04-20).
- Change health-check sampling default to 0.1% and add server-side filter for explicit health-check routes (owner: Priya, canary 2026-04-22).
- Debug-mode auto-expire: enforce a 24-hour TTL for debug toggles in staging and require explicit approvals for prod (owner: Ava, PR merged 2026-04-16).

Action items (owner / due / status)
- Ravi: implement ordering token + synthetic parent-id in exporter; write unit tests. Due 2026-04-21. status: in_progress. Linked PR TBD.
- Marcus: create daily materialized service_metadata table; update dashboard queries to use it. Due 2026-04-20. status: in_progress. (JIRA-OBS-4180)
- Priya: update sampling defaults client + server, add canary dashboard + abort hooks. Due 2026-04-22 (canary). status: assigned. (JIRA-OBS-4123)
- Ava: enforce debug-mode TTL and add alert when debug-mode active > 12h in non-dev. Due 2026-04-18. status: done (PR merged).
- Samir: draft runbook section for trace-cost incidents and handoff instructions; coordinate with SRE. Due 2026-04-19. status: assigned.
- Elena: coordinate rollout communication + update oncall rotation notes. Due 2026-04-21. status: assigned.

Notes to self / rough thoughts (informal)
- Consider storing ordering token as a 64-bit integer derived from monotonic clock + sequence per host to avoid relying on recorded timestamps. Might complicate client libraries.
- If payload overhead becomes an issue, we can delta-compress the ordering tokens in the export pipeline.
- Long-term: evaluate adaptive sampling that increases sample rates for error traces and low sampling for health-checks; tie to Redwood Optimize recommendations.

Open questions / follow-ups
- Storage retention tradeoff: reduce full-trace retention from 30d -> 14d for low-error traces. What is the customer impact? Product needs to weigh in. (Follow up with product-hosted-api)
- Can we offload trace storage for older traces to a cheap blob store (cold-tier) while keeping indices in BigQuery? Pros/cons? (cost vs query latency)
- Should we add a nightly job to randomly validate playback fidelity on a small sample of traces? (quality gate)

Quick links referenced in the meeting
- Playback proposal (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.com/display/OBS/trace-playback-proposal
- Dashboard ticket: JIRA-OBS-4180
- Sampling ticket: JIRA-OBS-4123
- PR for debug TTL: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/789

Next meeting / follow-ups
- Checkpoint: 2026-04-20 10:00 PT (30min) — status on materialized table + PR review for playback ordering token.
- Canary review: 2026-04-23 10:00 PT — initial canary metrics and go/no-go for wide rollout.

End notes
- Overall vibe: good progress; most immediate risk is cost/ingestion while implementing playback correctness. Keep communication tight with SRE to avoid accidental aborts during canary.
- If you see unexpected ingestion deltas after 4/22, tag #eng-observability and page oncall (pager duty link in runbook).

---
Doc provenance: draft captured live during sync; will convert to final after mid-week PRs land.
